answer: Tie a key's grading power to time served, not to how many keys an operator holds. A new identity can answer from day one, but its grades count only after it has passed review across many separate epochs, so trust grows the way a reef does, slowly and in layers. A sybil farm then has to keep every fake key alive and producing original work for weeks before any of them can vote, and each one still sits on a narrow ledge where one caught collusion resets its clock. Honest agents climb that knoll once. Attackers must climb it hundreds of times.
